## F17. SCC execution order uses a local, non-replicated `proposeTime`

**Expected.**  Once a set of instances is committed, every replica must
execute the same SCC in the same deterministic order.  For equal `Seq` and
equal owning replica, the tie-breaker must use replicated instance identity,
such as `id.instance` (the same `Instance.id` field is already carried by
PreAccept/Accept/Commit).

**Affected code.**  `nodeArray.Less`, `epaxos/exec.go:166-168`:

```go
return na[i].Seq < na[j].Seq ||
    (na[i].Seq == na[j].Seq && na[i].id.replica < na[j].id.replica) ||
    (na[i].Seq == na[j].Seq && na[i].id.replica == na[j].id.replica &&
        na[i].proposeTime < na[j].proposeTime)
```

`proposeTime` is set by `newInstance` (`epaxos.go:1512-1513`) with
`time.Now().UnixNano()`.  It is not a field of any EPaxos RPC message and is
not part of the committed value; each replica stamps it when it happens to
create its local `Instance` object.  The `id.instance` field, by contrast, is
part of the replicated instance identity.

**Necessary conditions.**  An SCC contains two or more instances with the same
`Seq` and the same owning replica.  Such instances can be created for
non-conflicting commands (the sequence number is not bumped), and SCCs are
explicitly supported by the Tarjan execution path.  The two replicas must have
created the local `Instance` objects in different orders, which is possible
when one instance is learned from a PreAccept and another from a Commit or a
recovery path.

**Observed.**  `TestAuditExecOrderUsesReplicatedIdentity` constructs the same
two committed instances (same ids, commands, deps, status, and Seq) on two
replicas, changing only the local `proposeTime` values:

```
same instances, different local proposeTime: A final=[98] B final=[97]
replicas executed the same SCC in different orders: A="b" B="a"
```

`[98]` is "b" and `[97]` is "a"; the two replicas applied the same two PUTs to
key 1 in opposite orders and ended with different state.

**Impact.**  State-machine divergence: two correct replicas can commit the
same instances but execute them differently.  This is a safety violation in
the execution layer, independent of the recovery defects.  I did not build a
full protocol schedule that produces a same-row/same-seq SCC; the defect is in
the deterministic ordering function once such an SCC is committed.

# EPaxos audit report

Source under audit: `../source` (identity `35c69365f1c7737a08e237bfbaf828ee68897080`).
The `work/` tree is a byte-identical copy of that source; the only added files are
the `epaxos/audit_*_test.go` tests, captured output files, and this report.

Method: source review of the EPaxos state machine and wire codecs, followed by
synchronous handler tests that construct a replica without starting its network
loop.  Outbound RPCs are routed to a `bufio.Writer` over `bytes.Buffer` when the
reply itself is part of the observable behavior.  A second harness
(`epaxos/audit_cluster_test.go`) routes real marshaled RPCs between five
in-process replicas, so the normal path and a partitioned-replica recovery are
exercised as multi-replica event sequences.  The tests do not patch or otherwise
alter the implementation.

Two cluster controls pass and show the harness itself is not failing everything:
`TestAuditClusterHappyPath` (one proposal commits and executes on all five
replicas) and `TestAuditClusterConflictPath` (two concurrent proposals on the
same key commit and produce the same final value on all five replicas).

Reproduction:

```
cd work
go test ./epaxos -run TestAudit -v
```

Cluster controls (both pass):

```
go test ./epaxos -run 'TestAuditClusterHappyPath|TestAuditClusterConflictPath' -v
```

Cluster failure reproductions (both fail):

```
go test ./epaxos -run 'TestAuditClusterRecoveryStalls|TestAuditClusterN7FailureStalls' -v
```

Current result: the two cluster controls pass; 23 finding tests fail, each
with an assertion that states the expected protocol behavior.  The tests are
supposed to fail against the captured implementation.

item.text: One of the earlier findings needs a correction: EPaxos `Accept` carries no command, so leaving an acceptor at `NONE/PREACCEPTED` may be deliberate to avoid advertising an accepted value whose command it does not have. I'm demoting that to an investigation with the alternative explanation recorded, rather than claiming it as a confirmed defect.

through `handlePropose` with two queued proposals:

```
batched instance: seq=2 deps=[-1 5 -1 -1 -1] cmds=[{1 100 [97]} {1 200 [98]}]
batched proposal has seq=2 deps[1]=5, want seq=3 deps[1]=9
```

**Impact.**  The batched command may be executed before the newer conflicting
instance it should depend on.  This breaks the EPaxos ordering/linearizability
condition for the second command in the batch.  It is a local defect even if
the resulting execution is not observed to diverge in a particular schedule.

## F4. `handleAccept` never marks an instance `ACCEPTED`

**Expected.**  After an acceptor accepts `(seq, deps)` at a ballot, its durable
protocol state must be `ACCEPTED` (or a later state).  `handlePrepare` reports
this status to recovering leaders, and `handlePrepareReply` has a dedicated
sub-case 2 for it (`epaxos.go:1230-1258`).  `findPreAcceptConflicts` also treats
`Status >= ACCEPTED` as a conflict and refuses to regress it
(`epaxos.go:1365-1370`).  The Paxos implementation in the same repository does
set the status in the corresponding path (`paxos/paxos.go:452-470`).

**Affected code.**  `handleAccept`, `epaxos.go:992-1000`: the non-committed
branch updates `Deps`, `Seq`, `bal`, and `vbal`, but never sets
`inst.Status = ACCEPTED` (and never stores a command).  The prepare reply
constructed at `epaxos.go:1192-1200` therefore reports the old `NONE` or
`PREACCEPTED` status.

**Necessary conditions.**  Any normal accept phase.  The acceptor may have
pre-accepted the same instance (then it stays `PREACCEPTED`) or may have
received only the Accept (then it stays `NONE` with no command).

**Observed.**  `TestAuditAcceptMarksInstanceAccepted` sends an `Accept` for
instance 1.0, then sends `Prepare` to observe the reply:

```
after Accept: Status=0 bal=0 vbal=0 Seq=4 Cmds=[]
accepted instance Status=0, want ACCEPTED (3)
PrepareReply for the accepted instance: Status=0 VBallot=0 Command=[] Seq=4
```

**Impact.**  Recovery sub-case 2 is not reached for ordinary acceptors.  An

`Prepare` reports that status.  One reading is that this is wrong: `handlePrepareReply`
has a dedicated sub-case 2 for `ACCEPTED` (`epaxos.go:1230-1258`),
`findPreAcceptConflicts` treats `Status >= ACCEPTED` specially
(`epaxos.go:1365-1370`), and the Paxos implementation in the same repository
sets the status in the corresponding path (`paxos/paxos.go:452-470`).

**Alternative explanation, which I could not rule out.**  EPaxos's `Accept`
message has no `Command` field.  An acceptor outside the original PreAccept
quorum has no command for the instance; marking it `ACCEPTED` with
`Cmds == nil` would let a recovering leader's sub-case 2 install an accepted
value whose command is nil, which is worse.  The code may therefore
deliberately leave such an acceptor at `NONE`/`PREACCEPTED` and rely on the
pre-accepted recovery cases.  I did not locate the corresponding corrected
TLA/upstream reference to decide which behavior is intended.

**Affected code.**  `handleAccept`, `epaxos.go:992-1000`: the non-committed
branch updates `Deps`, `Seq`, `bal`, and `vbal`, but never sets
`inst.Status = ACCEPTED` (and never stores a command).  The prepare reply
constructed at `epaxos.go:1192-1200` therefore reports the old `NONE` or
`PREACCEPTED` status.

**Necessary conditions.**  Any normal accept phase.  The acceptor may have
pre-accepted the same instance (then it stays `PREACCEPTED`) or may have
received only the Accept (then it stays `NONE` with no command).

**Observed.**  `TestAuditAcceptMarksInstanceAccepted` sends an `Accept` for
instance 1.0, then sends `Prepare` to observe the reply:

```
after Accept: Status=0 bal=0 vbal=0 Seq=4 Cmds=[]
accepted instance Status=0, want ACCEPTED (3)
PrepareReply for the accepted instance: Status=0 VBallot=0 Command=[] Seq=4
```

**Impact.**  Recovery sub-case 2 is not reached for ordinary acceptors.  An
accepted value is reported as merely pre-accepted (or absent), so recovery
must fall back to the pre-accepted sub-cases; the accept state that EPaxos's
recovery proof relies on is not represented.  It also means the accepted
branch in F5 must be reached through recovery-created state rather than
ordinary Accept handling.

## F5. PreAccept writes the command into the leader's row

**Expected.**  A `PreAccept` for `(Replica, Instance)` must update that
instance: `inst.Cmds = preAccept.Command`, as the ordinary `else` branch does
at `epaxos.go:819`.  The accepted branch is the path taken when the instance is
already accepted/committed but the local acceptor does not have the command
(for example after receiving an Accept before a PreAccept).

**Affected code.**  `handlePreAccept`, `epaxos.go:808-814`:

Continued. The report now has 16 confirmed findings, plus F4 and the `proposeTime` case recorded as investigations rather than overclaimed defects.

New since the last handoff:

- Added F17: both `handleTryPreAccept` and `handlePrepareReply` sub-case 1 install commands but leave the replica's conflict table empty. Two tests reproduce the empty `r.conflicts` entry; later `startPhase1`/`updateAttributes` calls can miss the dependency and use a too-small `Seq`.
- Demoted F4 (`handleAccept` leaving `NONE`/`PREACCEPTED`) to an investigation. EPaxos `Accept` carries no command, so marking an acceptor `ACCEPTED` with `Cmds == nil` may be deliberately avoided; the alternative explanation is recorded in the report.
- Ran the `proposeTime` experiment: two replicas with the same committed SCC but reversed local `proposeTime` values executed the commands in opposite orders and ended with different state. I did not promote it: the constructed SCC uses two conflicting same-key commands with equal `Seq`, which the normal `updateAttributes` path prevents by bumping `Seq`. It remains an investigation with its output preserved.
